# Mobile Cleanliness — Phase Two: Gevurah Evidence Gates

The Awtsmoos gives every glow a boundary, every menu a shore, every button a floor;
Awtsmoos.com should never make a user chase controls beyond the glass or guess what an unfinished tail is for.

## Evidence gate before any production rewrite

For each target, inspect git status first and treat concurrent modifications as protected. Read complete entry markup and every directly loaded stylesheet/script that controls layout or interaction. Then run a readiness-aware mobile probe only after the page's actual CSS and modules have loaded.

## Required mobile measurements

- `documentElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` at 390×844 and 320×568.
- Bounding boxes for fixed/sticky controls, open menus, drawers, dialogs, popovers, HUDs, and primary actions.
- Whether any visible interactive element has right > viewport width, left < 0, bottom > viewport height when it claims fixed positioning, or an unusably small touch target.
- Whether hidden/off-canvas elements are intentionally hidden and become fully contained when opened.
- Whether every expandable surface can close through keyboard/touch and returns focus predictably.
- Whether short-phone geometry still exposes the primary task rather than only chrome.

## CSS conflict scan

For candidate problem selectors, collect all declarations from loaded stylesheets and trace cascade order before changing source. Flag only proven conflicts such as width/min-width fights, duplicate positioning models, mutually incompatible display modes, or desktop rules that override later mobile rules.

## Interaction-state contract

Any production control with a transition or animation must have purposeful `:hover`, `:active`, and `:focus-visible` behavior when the platform supports them. Touch behavior may use pressed classes or `:active`; reduced-motion must neutralize nonessential transforms. Continuous ambient animation is allowed only when it is content, not control chrome.

## Rewrite threshold

Rewrite only when at least one of these is proven:
- off-screen interactive UI;
- document overflow caused by interface geometry;
- unintended overlap;
- inaccessible/unclear hidden menu state;
- obviously unstyled trailing section;
- conflicting CSS causing different breakpoints to fight;
- primary controls too small or unreachable;
- hover animation with no active/focus equivalent;
- desktop-only advanced panel permanently occupying mobile space.

Aesthetic preference alone is not enough to rewrite a working page.
